paragraphs.text: [Mi Lan Xiang](dancong:mi-lan-xiang) is one of the traditional ten types by which [Phoenix Dancong](dancong:definition) is sorted and sold, and one of the most widely made. Each type has its own name, and its character comes from the bush and the making, [not from anything added](dancong:aromas) to the leaf.

The leaf comes from Phoenix Mountain in Chaozhou, eastern Guangdong. [Dancong](dancong:name) means single bush: the leaf of one bush made on its own, though a named line today is mostly grown from cuttings or grafts of a chosen bush. This lot was given a medium [roast](dancong:making), and the roast is one of the main ways one Dancong differs from another.

brewing.text: Brew it gongfu style in a small gaiwan or clay pot, with about 3 to 8 grams for 100 to 120 ml and hot water, about 88 to 100°C; Chinese accounts mostly say 95 to 100°C. A quick rinse is common. Steeps start at a few seconds and grow a few seconds each round, and a good Dancong gives about eight to fifteen. Too long, too hot or too much leaf and it turns bitter and astringent.

notice.text: Flowers above all, a sweetness that comes back after swallowing, a high scent that lasts, honey, often ripe fruit such as peach, and what the trade calls mountain rhyme, shan yun; a liquor from golden to orange-red or amber.
